title: Member of Technical Staff (Site Reliability Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
description_html:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

 - Production Kubernetes at scale: cluster upgrades, CNI, CoreDNS, autoscalers like Karpenter, and debugging a misbehaving node at 3 a.m. Writing Helm charts alone doesn't count.

 - Terraform mastery. You've designed module structures, managed state across many accounts, and run large refactors and imports without taking production down.

 - Strong networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, load balancing, routing).

 - You write real code in Python, Go, or Rust for automation, tooling, and controllers, and you'd rather automate a runbook than follow it.

 - Fluency with observability tools like Datadog, Prometheus, or Grafana, and the judgment to turn metrics, logs, and traces into SLOs and alerts that matter.

 - A track record of leading production incidents and turning root-cause analysis into durable fixes.

 - You own problems end-to-end and do well when the path forward isn't laid out for you.




ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Multi-region active-active or failover architectures, and disaster-recovery programs with real recovery targets.

 - Proxies, service meshes, and kernel-level networking: Envoy, Istio, Cilium, or eBPF.

 - GitOps and progressive delivery: Argo CD, Flux, or similar.

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

 - Running stateful systems in production: Postgres, Redis, or search engines like Vespa or Elasticsearch.

 - Multi-cloud or neocloud operations (GCP, CoreWeave, or similar).

 - FinOps: cost attribution, Savings Plans and reservations, and making infrastructure cheaper without making it fragile.
$220K – $405K • Offers Equity

title: Sr. IAM Cybersecurity Engineer, Enterprise Identity
description_html: Your work days are brighter here.     We’re obsessed with making hard work pay off, for our people, our customers, and the world around us. As a Fortune 500 company and a leading AI platform for managing people, money, and agents, we’re shaping the future of work so teams can reach their potential and focus on what matters most. The minute you join, you’ll feel it. Not just in the products we build, but in how we show up for each other. Our culture is rooted in integrity, empathy, and shared enthusiasm. We’re in this together, tackling big challenges with bold ideas and genuine care. We look for curious minds and courageous collaborators who bring sun-drenched optimism and drive. Whether you're building smarter solutions, supporting customers, or creating a space where everyone belongs, you’ll do meaningful work with Workmates who’ve got your back. In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.           About the Team  The Enterprise Identity team sits within Workday's Cyber Security function as a key part of Enterprise Security. We are dedicated to delivering secure identity and access management, lifecycle management, governance and administration, and privileged access management to the entire Workday organization. We architect business processes, align enterprise tooling, document processes and procedures, and partner with peer organizations to keep Workday secure. Our team collaborates with key partners across the company, including Business Technology (BT), Product & Technology, Legal & Compliance, Internal Audit, and other Security organizations. In the year ahead, we are focused on advancing Identity Governance and driving Zero Standing Privileges initiatives that will help shape the future of identity security at Workday. We are a team that takes our mission seriously while fostering a collaborative and supportive environment. If you are passionate about identity security and want to make a meaningful impact at a global technology leader, this is the team for you!    About the Role     As technical lead for Workday’s User Access Review (UAR) strategy and execution, you’ll run end-to-end access certification programs, eliminate access creep, and keep governance and compliance continuous across IAM, ILM, IGA, and PAM systems.  In this role, you will:   Design, architect, and run enterprise-wide UAR programs to detect and remediate access creep across cloud and on-prem environments  Automate certification workflows and review cadences in IGA platforms to cut admin effort and improve accuracy  Partner with internal and external auditors to align UAR with SOX, SOC2, and ISO 27001, and deliver audit-ready reporting  Pair Zero Standing Privileges (ZSP) and Just-In-Time (JIT) provisioning with periodic reviews to speed revocation and enforce least privilege  Apply AI/ML to enable risk-based reviews, automated revocation suggestions, and anomaly detection  Build identity and security services with AI/ML to automate threat detection and risk-based access decisions  Work with product owners on secure requirements, security architecture, and contextual authorization  Evolve security policies and procedures toward modern, least-privilege identity approaches  Own identity security and governance across departments, influencing stakeholders at every level  Treat identity solutions as internal products, scaling them for efficiency and adoption  Balance strong security controls with business agility and a smooth user experience    Core focus: User Access Reviews.  UARs anchor Workday’s identity governance, keeping access aligned with least privilege. You’ll lead three pillars:    Strategy & governance:  Build certification cycles scaled to system criticality and risk, with clear entitlement ownership, definition catalogs, and automated revocation workflows   Automation & intelligence:  Use IGA platforms and AI/ML to reduce reviewer fatigue through peer-group analysis, usage signals, and automatic revocation of inactive entitlements   Compliance & audit readiness:  Standardize audit trails, evidence collection, and reporting (SOX, SOC2, ISO 27001) with full traceability of every review decision and access change      About You    Basic Qualifications  Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Security, or a related field  7+ years of IT or infosec experience (4+ with an MS)  Hands-on experience designing, launching, and managing enterprise-scale UAR and access certification campaigns  Experience with Okta (IAM, Workflows)  Deep expertise in IGA tooling (Okta Identity Governance, SailPoint, Saviynt) for automated UAR campaigns, entitlement cataloging, and remediation  Familiarity with identity lifecycle management concepts, including source of truth  Practical experience with regulatory compliance, audit readiness, and identity gap remediation  Other Qualifications   UAR & compliance mastery:  Orchestrating complex certifications across heterogeneous systems, mapping entitlements, and enforcing regulatory controls   Product mindset:  Focus on user experience, reduced friction, and measurable adoption alongside security   Risk-based judgment:  Sound decisions in ambiguous environments, balancing security and operational needs   Influence:  Strong communication from engineers to the C-suite; ability to translate identity risk into business impact   Security engineering & AI:  Experience building secure systems and applying AI/ML to risk scoring and access control   Threat & vulnerability management:  Assessing and mitigating weaknesses in identity infrastructure; staying current on threats   Core knowledge:  Zero Trust, identity management principles, and MFA, SSO, SAML, OIDC, and LDAP   Nice to have:  CISSP or equivalent     Workday Pay Transparency Statement      The annualized base salary ranges for the primary location and any additional locations are listed below.  Workday pay ranges vary based on work location. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the Workday Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission/bonus, as well as annual refresh stock grants. Recruiters can share more detail during the hiring process. Each candidate’s compensation offer will be based on multiple factors including, but not limited to, geography, experience, skills, job duties, and business need, among other things. For more information regarding Workday’s comprehensive benefits, please   click here  .      Primary Location: USA.VA.Reston    Primary Location Base Pay Range:  $159,600 USD - $239,400 USD    Additional US Location(s) Base Pay Range: $144,400 USD - $258,000 USD    Our Approach to Flexible Work      With Flex Work, we’re combining the best of both worlds: in-person time and remote. Our approach enables our teams to deepen connections, maintain a strong community, and do their best work. We know that flexibility can take shape in many ways, so rather than a number of required days in-office each week, we simply   spend at least half (50%) of our time each quarter in the office or in the field   with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.
